raw_response:
I am 51 this year, and I do things the way I have seen work here. I cannot read the technical papers, so I look at my own land, look at other people in the village, and follow what gives a steady harvest. On my 40 mu, wheat and maize go one after the other, same as usual. I have a well, so I am not fully depending on the sky, but pumping water costs money, so I will not water too many times unless the crop really needs it. For wheat, I will sow in early October after getting the land ready, use the seed people around here commonly buy, put a fair amount of fertilizer as base and then topdress once when the wheat starts growing strongly. I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than let the wheat turn yellow and lose yield. After wheat harvest in June, I will move fast to maize because the gap is short. I will not do fancy tillage, just quick field prep and sow hybrid maize right away. Maize usually needs less water than wheat here if summer rain is decent, so I will watch the weather and give one or two irrigations only if the field dries. My main thinking is simple: keep the land fully planted, do what worked nearby last year, do not spend too wildly, but do not save money in the wrong place and lose harvest.
